verification.note: Publisher pages read for each cited section; authors, place and date taken from the attribution block on the §19.4 page. §19.4 defines cardiac output as the blood pumped by each ventricle in one minute, CO = HR × SV, with a mean resting SV of about 70 mL for a 70-kg individual (range 55–100 mL), an average resting HR of about 75 bpm (60–100 in some individuals) and a mean CO of 5.25 L/min (range 4.0–8.0 L/min); as HR rises there is less time for the ventricles to fill, and above 160 bpm CO decreases as SV falls faster than HR increases. §20.2 defines systolic pressure as the arterial pressure during ventricular contraction (the higher value) and diastolic as the pressure during ventricular relaxation (the lower value), gives MAP ≈ diastolic + (systolic − diastolic)/3 with the 120/80 example ≈ 93.33, a normal MAP range of 70–110 mm Hg, pulse pressure as systolic minus diastolic, 120/80 as a normal adult blood pressure, blood flow = ΔP / resistance, viscosity, length and diameter as factors of resistance, resistance inversely proportional to radius to the fourth power, and the half-radius (16× resistance) and double-radius (1/16 resistance, 16× flow) examples.
supports: CO = HR × SV; SV ≈ 70 mL for a 70-kg individual (55–100 mL); HR ≈ 75 bpm (60–100); CO 5.25 L/min (4.0–8.0) (§19.4)
